## `zos.software`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

A software service instance running on a z/OS system, such as a CICS region, an IMS subsystem, or a batch job.

**Type:** `zos.software`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | [`mainframe.partition.name`](/docs/registry/mainframe/README.md#mainframe-partition-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the logical partition (LPAR) running on the mainframe. [1] | `LPAR01`; `PRODZ`; `TEST1` |
| Identity | [`zos.smf.id`](/docs/registry/zos/README.md#zos-smf-id) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The System Management Facilities (SMF) identifier that uniquely identifies a z/OS system within a sysplex or standalone mainframe environment. [2] | `SYS1`; `PROD1`; `TEST2` |
| Identity | [`zos.sysplex.name`](/docs/registry/zos/README.md#zos-sysplex-name) | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the z/OS systems complex (SYSPLEX) to which this z/OS system belongs. [3] | `SYSPLEX1`; `PRODPLEX` |

**[1] `mainframe.partition.name`:** A logical partition (LPAR) is the mainframe equivalent of a virtual machine (VM) in distributed cloud environments. Each LPAR can run an independent operating system such as z/OS, Linux, or z/VM. Reported by the HMC Web Services API partition object field `name`.

**[2] `zos.smf.id`:** The SMF system identifier (SMFID) is a 1-4 character alphanumeric name set at IPL time via the SMFPRMxx parmlib member. It is used throughout z/OS for system identification in SMF records, RMF reports, and sysplex routing.

**[3] `zos.sysplex.name`:** A sysplex is a cluster of z/OS systems that cooperate using the coupling facility (CF) for shared data and workload management. The sysplex name is defined in the COUPLExx parmlib member. In distributed systems terms, a sysplex is analogous to a high-availability cluster.
